deals.title: Palm Ventures - Hivemind
deals.next_step: Palm is aligning internally on scope and priorities before re-engaging. Follow up to re-engage once they've defined where to start.
deals.description:
Family office split between Connecticut and Texas (principal moved to TX, new team building there). First sales call Oct 28, 2026 with Johnny and Ryan; attendees Joshua (jfrumberg@palmventures.com), Rachel, Leigh and Daniela Plattner (palmventurestudios.com).

Opportunity: Hivemind as a central, permissioned "brain" across fragmented tools (Affinity CRM, email-heavy deal flow, Google, Outlook, Notion, Windows file server) so anyone can query deal status without interrupting colleagues. Starting focus is the sourcing and deals team; longer term, agents that understand their (non-SOP, messy) deal workflows.

Security-conscious and rolling AI out slowly. Joshua's three risks: data leakage, unauthorized external agent access, agents corrupting underlying data. Positioned Vertex walled-garden deployment, role-based permissioning mirroring the org chart, and workflow-layer filtering of what enters the Hivemind.

Pricing discussed: fully custom, $7,500/month minimum meaningful engagement; Hivemind setup with permissioned access as a fast, low-cost starting point.

deals.title: Infusion Health - Commercial AI
deals.next_step: Mike running solo discovery with Infusion's head of sales/marketing and CIO, then refining his opportunity report (~60% done) before introducing Supernal. Johnny to send Mike the milestone/KPI contract for reference (internal only).
deals.description:
Referral from Mike Rappaport (old friend of Ryan), who knows CEO Dan personally and is running pre-discovery before introducing Supernal. Prep call Oct 27, 2026 with Johnny, Ryan and Mike.

Company: ~$500M revenue, 5 years old, aggressive growth goals (multi-billion). Internal tech: CIO Scott Donahue plus 2 engineers (likely analytics/Power BI backgrounds) who built a nurse-facing Claude chatbot called Florence. A VP of AI Transformation (Dale Shim) appears on LinkedIn but Dan didn't mention him.

Pain points: commercialization is Dan's top priority; sales and marketing lagging on AI adoption; physician referral relationships untracked (no scoring or performance visibility); referral processing still manual via digital fax, which Dan ties directly to revenue. HIPAA and patient data involved.

Stakeholders: likely primary buyer is the head of sales and marketing (not yet named). Position Supernal as an "Iron Man suit" for the CIO, not a replacement. Dan is open on make vs buy. Milestone and KPI-based engagement should resonate. Johnny wants to approach the account holistically rather than as one-off point solutions.
